question: Identify the number of electrons found in the outermost shell of halogen.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Halogens have **seven electrons** in their outermost shell.
 
• They are located in Group 17 of the periodic table.
 
• Halogens include elements like fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, and astatine.
 
• These elements are highly reactive and are known for their ability to form salts when combined with metals.
 
• The seven valence electrons make them one electron short of a full octet, which explains their high reactivity.
